integrationDecisions: Keep existing 12 Galley foods, 37 Galley recipes, 30 soda recipes, tags and save IDs unchanged; the 240 rows are a separate proposed catalogue.
The current grain_mix item is Nutrifruit flour, not a generic grain. Add eight distinct grain IDs rather than renaming it or substituting one for every grain.
Chicken, Pork, Beef and Vatmeat are proposed expansion meats, not aliases for generic native raw meat. Preserve that distinction.

Map workbook Counter to the shared back-room counter; rack tier requires an owned crate in the first purchased rack slot; Water tank requires an installed Waterworks unit; Stove maps to a fitted galley; Refrigerator maps to a fitted native fridge.
A full cumulative kitchen needs three station bays (Waterworks, galley, fridge), compatible with the four-bay limit. Rack storage uses no station bay.
Workbook station recipes must be enabled by cumulative progress, not unlock every recipe immediately on buying a galley.
Workbook routine cooking water is supplied by the stove; current Galley consumes measured water and battery power. Resolve water portions, purity and energy costs before production registration.
Do not make unlimited free Water from a fitted tank. Draw from owned liquid and preserve its quality; define portion mL.
Workbook does not specify nutrition, prices, spoilage behavior, sprites, fixture install prices or power costs for new content. Existing economy and edible-state rules need deliberate values.
Keep refrigerator and Waterworks contents in their existing saved graphs. Do not duplicate them into a new kitchen inventory.
Small Morsel uses small_morsel for factory and runtime item identity; morsel_small is its sprite key.
Native meat/fish mappings use installed game code rather than relying on workbook external research pages. Supply availability is not proved by item factory existence.
implementationNote: 0.14: original chapter labels retained. Physical instrument and relevant heat/cold equipment determine access; no cumulative storage or Waterworks tier gates.
